“Violence is not chaos. It is judgment.”

Clan: Brujah · Generation: 8th · Sect: Camarilla · Sire of: @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (Haiti, 1960) and @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell} (Marseille, 1972)

Background character: he doesn't appear in the adventure and has no character sheet. Main source: doc 23, “🩸 Sire of David Smith: Marcus ‘Ironjaw’ Vance” (earlier source), supplemented by docs 00–16.

Vance is not in Seattle. Every sign of him is false. What is real is Krell, the other son, the one who wasn't chosen (doc 01).

  • The journals. In 1986, a year after his disappearance in the Carpathians, a middleman from Lyon sold the Brujah's journals at a private auction. Vance had asked for his havens to be burned. Someone didn't do it. The buyer was @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, who had three typewritten copies made (by Mr. Pell, @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}) and kept the original in his vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}). Copy 1 is in the vault, Krell has copy 2, and Halloway sent copy 3 to Justicar Panhard in 2025. Nobody in Seattle knows this except O'Connor (@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor}).
  • The ghost. With the journals, Halloway hires Krell, a Brujah whom Vance trained and abandoned in the '70s, who destroys Kindred by imitating Controlled Fury: so that David chases a dead man and Montgomery distrusts him. Halloway spreads the rumor “Vance, the Hound's sire, is back in town” through Krell.
  • Vance's coat reached Halloway in the same lot as the journals; Krell wears it in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}.
  • Clues and documents: @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)} (folio 14, Marseille 1963), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.xQqepYpthm1bxP8u]{Halloway Knows About the Cold Water} (Halloway quotes a line of Vance's that appears only in the journals), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard} (the inverted guard), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.TOvLdg2zhgDzjOAG]{The Journals Bought in 1986} (the journals bought in 1986), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} (folios 41 and 42 on “the German”), @UUID[JournalEntry.9zcPuCCutNfUtYJ0]{Vance's Lineage Tree} (lineage tree).
  • The forged letter. Halloway gives Montgomery a letter signed “M.V.” addressed to David. The handwriting is a near-perfect match for Vance's, but it's in English: Vance wrote his journals in French (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}).
  • Montgomery knew of Vance by reputation and genuinely fears him (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}).
  • Krell went looking for him in Cluj in '87: “There was nothing. Not even ash.”
  • The doctrine of Controlled Fury is @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury}: “Locate. Assess. Execute.”
  • Hooks: @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.Y1E4i0kdsA7wcPIj]{GAN-10 · Letters from Cluj} (letters from Cluj signed “M. V.”) and @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls} (Archon Duval, who knew Vance, read copy 3).

Marcus Vance was a World War II veteran, an artillery commander and military strategist who, after his Embrace in the '40s by an exiled European Brujah, became a figure of order and discipline within the clan—a rarity among his kind.

Unlike chaotic or idealistic Brujah, Marcus believed that revolution needed structure, and violence, purpose. In his view, the Masquerade was the wall that held the balance between Cainite anarchy and total extinction.

During the Cold War, he operated as a roving enforcer for the Camarilla, hunting Kindred who threatened political stability. His nickname, Ironjaw, came as much from his iron jaw as from his unbreakable resolve: he never backed down, not from humans and not from Elders.

Nicknames: Ironjaw, The Red Commander, The Hammer of Order · Years active: 1940–1985 · Place of origin: New York, USA · Last known location: Port-au-Prince, Haiti—1960 · Fate: Presumed destroyed by the Sabbat in the '80s, though unconfirmed. · Sect: Camarilla (missing, possibly hunted by the Inquisition).

Date: July 8, 1960 · Place: Haiti, during a covert SEAL mission.

David, then an American commando, was leading an infiltration operation on the Haitian coast, investigating a string of disappearances tied to blood cults. His squad was ambushed—not by rebels, but by a Sabbat pack that had turned the place into an experimentation camp.

Marcus Vance was in the area, hunting the same group on Camarilla orders. He arrived too late to save Smith's platoon… but in time to watch the young soldier, gravely wounded, refuse to die, dragging himself forward with a knife in hand to take out the last enemy even as he bled out.

“I saw something in him I hadn't seen in decades—not fear, not fury. I saw will. And I thought: men like that must not die. They must be used.” — Excerpt from the memoirs of Marcus Vance, recovered from his haven in Marseille.

Marcus Embraced him not out of compassion but out of strategic principle: David was the ideal soldier, a being with discipline, conscience, and an unbreakable moral code. He shaped him for a decade, teaching him the balance between the violence of the Beast and the structure of duty. Thus was born “the Hound of the Masquerade,” an enforcer deadlier and more precise than any Archon.

In 1985, Marcus Vance disappeared in Eastern Europe while investigating a Sabbat outbreak in Romania. Rumor among the Kindred says he was destroyed in direct combat with a Tzimisce Elder, though some reports link him to the Black Hand.

David never confirmed his death. But he still keeps the military knife he carried on the day of his Embrace, a relic of the moment he died as a human and was born as a hunter.

• Emotional bond: absolute respect, without sentimentality.
  • Blood Bond: dissolved decades ago, but the philosophical loyalty persists.
  • Influence: Marcus's voice still echoes in David's mind when he faces hard moral decisions.
  • Legacy: “Violence is not chaos. It is judgment.”

Doc 23 includes a portrait of Vance (image not exported).

📜 CONFIDENTIAL FILE—CAMARILLA / CLAN BRUJAH

Classification: SECRET—For active Justicars and Archons only

Reference: Dossier V-8A-BRUJAH / VANCE.M

Status: Missing—Presumed destroyed (1985)

Date of last verification: August 22, 1985, Romania

🩸 Kindred Identification

Name: Marcus Vance

Known aliases: Ironjaw, The Red Commander, The Hammer of Order

Clan: Brujah

Generation: 8th

Sect: Camarilla

Position: Roving enforcer under the mandate of Justicar Helena Panhard (1950–1979) (@UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Justicar Helena Panhard})

Known residences: Marseille, Vienna, Berlin, Port-au-Prince (temporary operation)

Current status: Missing. Last confirmed transmission: Transylvania sector, Romania.

⚰️ Chronological Data

Event Date Detail
Mortal birth 1911 New York, USA—family of Irish descent.
Mortal service 1931–1945 U.S. Army, Artillery Commander. Confirmed participation in the Normandy landings.
Embrace 1945 (Berlin) Embraced by an anonymous veteran Brujah after liberating a concentration camp—a symbolic act of redemption.
Age at death 34 Optimal physical condition, record of exceptional discipline.
True age (last record) 74 Appearance unchanged since his Embrace.
Last recorded mission 1985 Covert operation against the Black Hand in the Carpathians. Never returned.

⚔️ Blood Profile

  • Blood Potency: 5
  • Dominant Resonance: Pure Choleric—aggression channeled into control and discipline.
  • Estimated Humanity: 5 (strong inclination toward duty, but growing emotional detachment).
  • Predator: Guardian of Order (classic version of “Hunter of Hunters”).
  • Recorded Willpower: 8 (near-unbreakable resolve).

💀 Career and Historical Significance

Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance stood out among the Brujah for his unusual loyalty to the Camarilla and his devotion to the Masquerade as a principle of survival. While others of his clan championed revolution, Marcus championed order. He was an old-school soldier: he believed in hierarchy, discipline, and force as the language of justice.

“Where others see rebellion, I see indiscipline. The Beast does not need to be free. It needs to be tamed.” — Marcus Vance, Marseille, 1973.

During the Cold War, he acted as a roving agent of the Camarilla, eliminating Sabbat cells, Anarch heresies, and uncontrolled vampires in conflict zones. His modus operandi was direct and surgical: “Locate. Assess. Execute.”

Vance was a mentor and, to some, an executioner. His reputation was that of an incorruptible enforcer, feared even by the Ventrue he served.

🩸 The Embrace of David Smith

In 1960, during a joint operation with agents of the Sheriff of New Orleans, Vance intercepted a Sabbat pack in Haiti. There he found a dying young commando: David Smith, sole survivor of a platoon devoured by the enemy Cainites.

According to reports recovered from his hermetic journal (Marseille, 1963):

“Not all men deserve to die. Some only need a different war. Smith did not ask to be saved. But he did not surrender either. That is enough.”

He Embraced Smith to forge a living weapon against vampiric indiscipline. For nearly a decade he trained him under a martial code: obedience, precision, and restraint of the Beast. The Archons of Paris describe their relationship as “father and son in death.”

⚠️ Internal Assessment

Trait Assessment
Loyalty to the Camarilla Absolute (never questioned)
Threat level Lethal only if set against a Justicar's direct authority
Autonomy High; avoided fixed havens and clan structures
Psychology Cold, analytical; obsessive profile centered on discipline and emotional control
Known weakness Inability to delegate. Extreme belief in “duty before emotion”

🕯️ Fate and Legacy

Vance's last recorded communication dates to 1985, an encrypted message addressed to Archon Duval (@UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Archon Duval}):

“If I do not return, burn my havens. Whatever is left of me will no longer serve order.”

No physical remains were found. He is presumed destroyed in a confrontation with a Tzimisce Elder near Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Black Hand files confirmed activity in the area 48 hours later.

🔖 Documented Legacy

  • Founder of the “Controlled Fury” doctrine used by Camarilla Brujah hunters.
  • Mentor of David Smith, current enforcer for the Sheriff of Seattle.
  • Forerunner of the tactical training model for operational Kindred (1958–1978).

“He wasn't looking for soldiers. He was looking for monsters with a conscience.” — David Smith, private remark, 2004.

📎 Annex—Note from Archon Duval (2021)

“If Vance lives, he does so in absolute silence. If he died, his echo still resounds in every hunter who does not kill for pleasure. Either way, the Camarilla owes him the night.”

• Fate. The header of doc 23 says “presumed destroyed by the Sabbat in the '80s”; the dossier and docs 00–16 set it in 1985, near Cluj-Napoca. They agree on the essentials.
  • Journals. Doc 23 cites “memoirs recovered from his haven in Marseille” and a “hermetic journal (Marseille, 1963)” as if they were in Camarilla archives. In docs 00–16 the journals weren't burned; they were sold in 1986 and Halloway has them; the Camarilla has had only copy 3, since 2025 (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls}). The doc 23 quotes are not folio 14 of @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}.
  • David's training. Doc 23 says “for a decade” (nearly a decade in the dossier); docs 00–16 give no duration. Vance trained Krell in Marseille from 1972 to 1976 (@UUID[JournalEntry.9zcPuCCutNfUtYJ0]{Vance's Lineage Tree}), which doc 23 doesn't mention.
  • Controlled Fury. Doc 23 names it as Vance's doctrine, as does @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} (which places it in the 1950s).
